around.text: Gunmen held hostages in a Cartagena supermarket after an armoured-car raid failed.
Casualties hit a five-year high of 7,000, the annual Landmine Monitor found; Myanmar and Syria topped the list.
Hackers breached an unclassified CIA computer system; officials said no classified data was compromised.

cards.body: Asian shares tumbled — South Korea's Kospi fell as much as 5.3%, Taiwan 5.1% and Japan's Nikkei 2.9% — as the AI rally faded, Nvidia shedding 5.9%. Washington is poised to unveil new tariffs after an “excess capacity” probe of 16 trading partners.
cards.headline: Markets slide as US tariff threat returns

cards.body: A federal jury convicted China's Huawei and three subsidiaries on 10 of 12 counts — bank and wire fraud, Iran sanctions violations and stealing US trade secrets — after a three-month trial. It was acquitted of racketeering conspiracy.
cards.headline: Huawei convicted in New York trial

cards.body: China launched the Shenzhou-24 crew to its Tiangong space station carrying a Pakistani astronaut into orbit for the first time, deepening the two allies' partnership in space.
cards.headline: Shenzhou-24 flies first Pakistani astronaut

cards.body: Rescuers in West Java searched for about 30 workers trapped since Monday in a flooded, unauthorised gold mine in the Pongkor hills near Bogor.
cards.headline: Race to free miners trapped 100 m down

cards.body: Consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September and a fourth increase in a row, as fuel and energy costs climbed, the Office for National Statistics said.
cards.headline: UK inflation climbs to one-year high

cards.body: Australia's government formally apologised in parliament to current and former LGBTQ service members for decades of discriminatory policies, Defence Minister Richard Marles said.
cards.headline: Canberra apologises to LGBTQ veterans

footer: Compiled from the day's reporting by Reuters, AFP, Al Jazeera, Channel NewsAsia, SCMP, The Japan Times and the US Department of Justice

lead.body: A Houthi drone hit the 80-storey PIF Tower, home to Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund in the King Abdullah Financial District, wounding 11 people. The Saudi-led coalition condemned a “cowardly terrorist attack” in the war with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, reignited in July.
lead.caption: The 385-metre PIF Tower, Riyadh's tallest building — also hit last Thursday
lead.headline: Riyadh's tallest tower hit again
